lockOwnership.checks: fstat(fd)==stat(path) dev+ino; FLOCK WRITE line for that inode in /proc/<pid>/fdinfo/<fd> (OWNERSHIP); FLOCK WRITE for the inode in /proc/locks (liveness); optional --probe-lock-contention independent flock -n -x must be REFUSED
lockOwnership.correctionMade: The prior closure required the /proc/locks holder pid to be self-or-ancestor. MEASURED on this kernel (6.17.0-1026-nvidia): a flock belongs to the OPEN FILE DESCRIPTION and /proc/locks records the pid that CREATED it — the transient flock(1), already dead — so a genuinely inherited lock was misread as 'somebody else's'. Ownership authority moved to /proc/<pid>/fdinfo/<fd>; the /proc/locks pid is now recorded (procLock, procLockCreatorInAncestry) but is not the test.

invocationNotes: `exec 9>lock; flock -n -x 9; exec node` is required: the shell acquires the lock and then EXECS node, so the lock is never dropped before node starts and node itself becomes the holder of the open file description.
`flock -x lock -c 'node ...'` is acceptable to the kernel but the fd number is undocumented; `flock -o` would CLOSE the descriptor and must never be used.

This invocation is NOT authorised now: verifier-control.json activeRole is handoff-standby-verifier and the probe correctly refuses (exit 3, no browser). It also needs the shared heavy lock, which belongs to that other role right now.

Recorded in the decision's own `note` field rather than being claimed as full byte coverage.
